variables.name: Tropospheric NO2
variables.definition: Nitrogen dioxide in the lower atmosphere, mostly from traffic and industry; a sign of air pollution.
variables.explanation: Tropospheric NO2 is decreasing by about 0.298 10¹⁵ molecules/cm² per decade (95% range: -0.67 to +0.15) over 22.1 years. No statistically significant trend was detected (FDR-adjusted p = 0.060). As a rough estimate, if this rate and noise level continue, a record of about 37 years in total would be needed to detect it (we have 22.1). Not significant does not mean no change.
variables.naive_vs_correct: The simple regression and the corrected test agree here.

variables.name: Air temperature at 500 hPa
variables.definition: Air temperature about 5.5 km above the ground (the 500 hPa pressure level), measured from space by AIRS.
variables.explanation: Air temperature at 500 hPa is increasing by about 0.378 °C per decade (95% range: +0.121 to +0.624) over 24.1 years. This trend is statistically significant (FDR-adjusted p < 0.001).
variables.naive_vs_correct: A simple regression on the raw data misses this trend because the seasonal cycle hides it; after removing the seasonal cycle, the corrected tests find it. Simple methods can also miss real trends.

variables.name: Air temperature (2 m)
variables.definition: The air temperature 2 meters above the ground: the temperature we feel.
variables.explanation: Air temperature (2 m) is increasing by about 0.619 °C per decade (95% range: +0.399 to +0.861) over 26.7 years. This trend is statistically significant (FDR-adjusted p < 0.001).
variables.naive_vs_correct: A simple regression on the raw data misses this trend because the seasonal cycle hides it; after removing the seasonal cycle, the corrected tests find it. Simple methods can also miss real trends.
